transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-11-19
Time: 14:00 PST
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Gwen Miller (CISO, Lakeshore), Raj Patel (Head of IT), Sophie Nguyen (Security Engineer), Tom Alvarez (Legal), Ava Brooks (Compliance)

--- Auto Summary (generated) ---
Short: SOC 2 / ISO posture review, confirm availability of attestation and evidence, Trust Center access, SSO, audit logs, data residency and KMS. Next steps agreed: share reports, controls mapping, schedule technical dive.

--- Topics ---
0. SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 scope
1. Trust Center access and evidence export
2. RBAC, SSO (SAML) and provisioning
3. Audit logs retention and SIEM integration
4. Data residency / region options and dedicated/private setups
5. Encryption, KMS/HSM integration and key management

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood Inference. With me is Daniel Park, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Gwen Miller: Hi Maya, thanks. We're doing OK, bit pressed, we have an external vendor assessment in early December so wanted to double check Redwood's artifacts.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Totally, that's the purpose. We prepared the SOC 2 Type II and ISO controls mapping, we'll go over what we can share and the mechanics to access evidence via our Trust Center.
[00:28] Raj Patel: Quick question up front—are those documents up to date for 2026? We need the latest period covering June through October ideally.
[00:36] Daniel Park: Yeah, the Type II covers the period through September 30, 2026. The ISO scope doc is aligned with that window as well, I believe. I'll confirm exact dates in the mapping doc we share.
[00:46] Gwen Miller: Good, because our auditor will want to see test procedures and evidence for controls, access lists etc. How do we get the raw evidence?
[00:56] Maya Chen: We can grant read-only access to the Trust Center where evidence bundles are stored; exports are available for specific controls. You can download attestations, sample configs, audit logs excerpts. We don't give direct database or backup access, obviously.
[01:12] Sophie Nguyen: When you say audit logs excerpts, is that full event log or filtered? Also retention—what's default and can it be extended?
[01:22] Daniel Park: By default we retain structured audit logs for 90 days in the hosted offering; we have options for longer retention in Dedicated and Private deployments, and long-term archives via S3 export policies. For the trust center evidence we typically provide filtered extracts tied to control IDs rather than full tails, to avoid PII exposure.
[01:38] Gwen Miller: Ok, that helps. On SSO—we run SAML via Okta and need SCIM provisioning for user sync. Does Redwood support SCIM?
[01:47] Maya Chen: Yes, we support SAML for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. For Dedicated and Private we also support IdP-initiated flows and allow provisioning via SCIM v2. There might be a small connector needed for some legacy Okta setups, Daniel can run through that.
[02:02] Daniel Park: Quick add: we expose RBAC at the token and per-route level; you can map Okta groups to roles in the Console. There was a small misdoc in the appendix of one of our older guides but it's updated—I'll send the corrected runbook.
[02:16] Raj Patel: About encryption, we need to confirm keys are customer-managed for our private deployment, and HSM backends—are those supported?
[02:26] Daniel Park: For Private deployments you can bring your own KMS. We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and external HSMs via KMIP in our private appliance. For Dedicated we offer customer-managed keys via AWS KMS in some regions; hosted tenants use Redwood-managed keys but with envelope encryption and enterprise options for CMKs on request.
[02:45] Gwen Miller: So for our audit we need an affirmation that keys are rotated and we can get key rotation logs.
[02:52] Maya Chen: Yes, key rotation metadata is available; we can provide key rotation records and attestations for rotations that occurred during the reporting window. The Trust Center contains those artifacts or we can export a CSV.
[03:04] Tom Alvarez: Any legal caveats about access to evidence? We need to ensure NDAs or data processing addendums are respected when we download artifacts.
[03:13] Maya Chen: Absolutely. Access is governed by our DPA and any existing contracts; Trust Center access is read-only and we log who downloaded evidence. We can provision access to named users only.
[03:24] Ava Brooks: Data residency—our policy requires EU data residency for EU customers. Can Redwood isolate processing in eu-west-1 or similar?
[03:33] Daniel Park: Yes, we support regional deployments. Hosted can pin the region for your tenant, and Dedicated provides capacity in specified cloud regions. Private gives you full control. Note that some model variants or certain GPUs might only be in select regions—I'll include a region/model compatibility note.
[03:50] Gwen Miller: On controls mapping—do you map to SOC Trust Services Criteria and also to ISO 27001 Annex A controls? Auditor wants mapping to both.
[03:58] Maya Chen: We maintain a dual mapping: SOC 2 control IDs crosswalked to NIST/ISO references. We'll share the controls mapping spreadsheet with each control, evidence artifact ID, and the Trust Center path.
[04:09] Sophie Nguyen: Regarding audit logs—can we forward logs to our SIEM? We use Splunk Cloud.
[04:17] Daniel Park: Yes, we have log forwarders and a syslog/S3 integration. For hosted tenants we provide a push/export agent that can send logs to a customer-owned S3 bucket or directly to Splunk via HTTP Event Collector. For Dedicated we can set up a private forwarder in the VPC.
[04:31] Raj Patel: Any PII redaction in logs? We can't allow raw PHI to go out.
[04:38] Daniel Park: We support field-level redaction and masking for logs; by default we exclude request payloads that contain user content from long-term logs. For compliance heavy customers we recommend Dedicated or Private where you control what gets forwarded.
[04:52] Gwen Miller: Can you explain what evidence looks like for change control and incident response? Our auditors want runbooks, ticket IDs, timelines.
[05:01] Maya Chen: Typical evidence bundles include change control tickets, deployment diffs, incident postmortem redacted for sensitive info, and timestamps. For incidents we provide a redacted postmortem and timeline, plus remediation actions. Again access is controlled.
[05:18] Tom Alvarez: Anything on penetration testing? Do you allow customer-led pentests or require vendor assisted?
[05:24] Daniel Park: We have an annual third-party pentest and a responsible disclosure program. For customer-led tests we have a request process and scoping; usually for Hosted we limit direct pentests to the customer's tenant scope and require coordination to avoid cross-tenant impact. For Private you can run tests freely within your environment.
[05:40] Gwen Miller: Good. On contractual SLA and security attestations—are the SOC 2 Type II and ISO certificate available to customers under NDA?
[05:48] Maya Chen: Yes, you get the Type II attestation and ISO certificate under NDA via the Trust Center, and we can provide SOC 3 high-level summary publicly.
[05:56] Ava Brooks: For the Trust Center access, what's the TTL on a link? Can we provision read-only users with time-bound access?
[06:03] Daniel Park: Yes, link TTLs and time-bound user roles are supported. We can grant 30-day read-only access or custom windows. Every download is logged.
[06:12] Sophie Nguyen: A small technical ask—our auditor wants the control mapping IDs to match their framework. Can you include control evidence IDs in the spreadsheet?
[06:20] Maya Chen: Yes, the spreadsheet includes columns: Redwood control, mapped SOC ID, mapped ISO Annex A ID, evidence artifact ID, Trust Center path.
[06:29] Raj Patel: On Dedicated vs Private—cost aside, our main driver is isolating logs and keys. Are there any feature gaps moving to Private?
[06:37] Daniel Park: Functionally Private mirrors Dedicated but with full network control; some managed conveniences like auto-updates are opt-in. We can provide a feature parity matrix.
[06:47] Gwen Miller: Any EU-specific certifications beyond ISO? Data residency plus local processing certifications?
[06:54] Maya Chen: We have support for regional compliance and can surface specific controls for GDPR; for local certification—depends on partner regions. We'll add a note.
[07:03] Tom Alvarez: For the legal team—if we pull evidence, can Redwood redact any customer-specific data? We may need that for vendor sharing.
[07:13] Maya Chen: Yes we redact customer-specific PIIs and provide redacted artifacts. If specific fields need removal we can tailor exports.
[07:22] Sophie Nguyen: One more: is there an API to pull evidence programmatically for automated audits?
[07:28] Daniel Park: We have a Trust Center API for evidence retrieval with proper auth and logging. It's rate-limited and scoped by control.
[07:36] Gwen Miller: Ok... this is helpful. Our path—auditor is on 12/08 so we need these artifacts in the next two weeks.
[07:44] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll prioritize the Type II report, the mapping spreadsheet, and the Trust Center link.
[07:50] Raj Patel: Could you also include a short data flow diagram showing where redwood touches PHI and what is in flight/out of scope?
[07:59] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll add a data flow diagram and a recommended configuration for minimizing PHI in logs.
[08:06] Gwen Miller: Great. Any blockers on our end?
[08:09] Ava Brooks: We'll need to sign a narrow NDA addendum to permit evidence download. I'll draft and send today.
[08:16] Tom Alvarez: From legal I'll review but likely fine.
[08:19] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll wait for the NDA then grant access.
[08:23] Daniel Park: For the technical deep-dive, propose we cover VPC peering, KMS configuration, and log forwarding—30 to 45 minute session.
[08:33] Sophie Nguyen: Prefer evening PST, but can do Tue/Wed next week.
[08:38] Daniel Park: I'll send a Doodle for options.
[08:41] Maya Chen: Ok let's recap.
[08:43] --- Recap ---
[08:44] Maya Chen: Action items: I'll send the SOC 2 Type II and controls mapping, grant Trust Center read-only access; Daniel will schedule the technical deep-dive for VPC/KMS and send corrected runbook for RBAC/SCIM; Sophie will share audit scope; Ava will send NDA addendum.
[09:02] Gwen Miller: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:06] Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up and get those artifacts over.
[09:10] (call ends)
